prompt.en: Which candidate becomes the MP for an electoral district?
prompt.fr: Quel candidat devient le député d'une circonscription électorale?

options.en: The one who finishes second in that district.
options.fr: Celui qui arrive deuxième dans cette circonscription.

options.en: The one whose party wins the most seats across Canada.
options.fr: Celui dont le parti remporte le plus de sièges dans l'ensemble du Canada.

options.en: The one with the most votes in that district.
options.fr: Celui qui obtient le plus de voix dans cette circonscription.

options.en: The one the Prime Minister chooses.
options.fr: Celui que le premier ministre choisit.

explanation.en: Voters mark one ballot, for a candidate and a party in their own district. The candidate ahead of the others wins the seat, even without half the votes. No ballot asks you to choose a Prime Minister; that office goes to the leader of the party that holds the confidence of the House of Commons.
explanation.fr: Les électeurs remplissent un seul bulletin, pour un candidat et un parti dans leur propre circonscription. Le candidat qui devance les autres remporte le siège, même sans obtenir la moitié des voix. Aucun bulletin ne vous demande de choisir un premier ministre; cette fonction revient au chef du parti qui a la confiance de la Chambre des communes.

source.quote: The people in each electoral district vote for the candidate and political party of their choice. The candidate who receives the most votes becomes the MP for that electoral district.

verification.evidence: The people in each electoral district vote for the candidate and political party of their choice. The candidate who receives the most votes becomes the MP for that electoral district. … Ordinarily, after an election, the leader of the political party with the most seats in the House of Commons is invited by the Governor General to form the government. After being appointed by the Governor General, the leader of this party becomes the Prime Minister. … The Prime Minister and the party in power run the government as long as they have the support or confidence of the majority of the MPs.
